sections.title: Interview bank U07: Linear attention, SSMs, FFT

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: 2T^2 d FLOPs, T^2 score memory; doubling T is 4x.
h_t = A h_{t-1} + B x_t; A controls memory decay and stability.
Associative combine: O(n) work, O(log n) depth.
Conv(x,k) = IFFT(FFT(x)*FFT(k)); direct wins for short kernels.

recall.question: Write the quadratic attention FLOP and memory formulas. What happens when T doubles?
recall.answer: 2T^2 d FLOPs per matmul, T^2 floats of scores. Doubling T multiplies both by 4.

recall.question: Write the SSM recurrence with shapes. What does A control?
recall.answer: h_t = A h_{t-1} + B x_t, y_t = C h_t. A: (N,N) controls memory decay and stability.

recall.question: Write the stability growth formula. What parameterization keeps A stable?
recall.answer: Growth A^n. Keep A stable via exp discretization of a negative continuous A, or eigenvalues inside the unit disk.

sections.title: Deep ladder 1: from quadratic to linear

keyTerms.definition: (2T)^2 = 4T^2: both FLOPs and memory scale with T^2.
phi(Q)(phi(K)^T V): O(T d^2) time, O(d^2) state.
What the kernel approximation breaks on: exact copy needs one-hot rows.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 computes the quadratic attention cost at T=8192, d=128, one head. What are the numbers?
recall.answer: 17.2 TFLOPs scores, 256 MiB fp32 score memory per head. Linear regroup: O(T d^2) time, O(d^2) state: 64x fewer FLOPs on the toy.

keyTerms.definition: Recurrence, convolution view, scan: one output, three forms.
Kernel taps K_k = C A^k B.
Input-dependent A: no single kernel exists; scan wins.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 unrolls the SSM triple identity on A=0.9, B=C=1, x=[1,0,1,0]. What are the states and the kernel?
recall.answer: States [1.0, 0.9, 1.81, 1.629]. Kernel [1, 0.9, 0.81, 0.729]. All three views compute the same recurrence output.

keyTerms.definition: 65,504: the 1.01 model crosses it at n=1115.
SSM state 64x smaller than attention scores on the toy.
Materializing every state to HBM destroys the SSM advantage.

recall.question: Stability: A=0.99 vs A=1.01 over 1000 steps. At what step does the 1.01 model cross fp16 max (65,504)?
T=8192, d=128: compare attention score bytes vs an SSM with N=64 fp32 state. What destroys the SSM advantage?
recall.answer: Scores: 134,217,728 bytes. SSM stream: 2,097,152. State: 32,768. Ratio 64x. An unfused eager loop destroys it by materializing every state to HBM.

keyTerms.definition: The bug: raw FFT product is circular, not linear.
Zero-pad both to 2n before transforming.

recall.question: D1. The FFT convolution disagrees with the naive result. What is the bug, the fix, and the theorem’s padding requirement?
recall.answer: Bug: the raw FFT product is the circular convolution, not the linear one. Fix: zero-pad both to length 2n. The theorem needs linear convolution; padding makes the circular result coincide with it.

keyTerms.definition: With infinite SRAM the choice is T^2 d vs T d^2 plus exact recall.
Causality relaxes: bidirectional is legal.
Usually a bidirectional encoder or chunked attention.

recall.question: SRAM is infinite. Does the SSM still beat attention?
recall.answer: The traffic argument dies but FLOPs do not: attention still costs T^2 d vs T d^2, and exact pairwise routing still needs the matrix. SSM wins on FLOPs at long T; attention wins on exact recall.

recall.question: The task is offline scoring of fixed documents (no generation). What relaxes, and what is cheapest?
recall.answer: Causality relaxes: bidirectional kernels and full attention are legal. The cheapest accurate choice is usually a bidirectional encoder-style model or chunked attention, not a causal SSM.

keyTerms.definition: Were recall probes included? Smooth-tasks-only invalidates.
Tested at train length only invalidates.

recall.question: A paper claims “linear attention matches softmax on all long-context benchmarks.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Recall probes included? (2) Sharp selection tasks? (3) Matched FLOPs? (4) Length generalization? (5) Seeds?
